_note: Race-day form (GDD 4.8 'Form'). Sharpness 0-100 is built by race-specific sessions (the `sharp` value on each session in training.json, and race_session in competitions.json) and fades by `decay` every day. Form on race morning, as a share of race time (+ = faster): a sharpness term (at_zero at sharpness 0, 0 at `neutral`, +cap at cap_at x neutral) plus a freshness term (+max at fatigue <= full_below, falling to 0 at zero_at), capped by total.max / total.min. `neutral` is calibrated (tools/form_check.gd) so the old repeating coach week averages 0 form over its races. Words: first match from the top by min (share of time); 'tired' (fatigue above tired_above) wins over all. color = hex.

ui.title: RACE FORM
ui.today_hint: How you would race if you raced today. Tap to see what builds it.
ui.explain: Form is a small boost or drag on your race time (about 1 % at most). It comes from sharpness (recent race-pace work) and freshness (low fatigue). What helps:

words.name: Peaking
words.text: You're sharp and fresh: the best shape you can race in.
words.helps: Race-specific work (800 m intervals, club sessions, races) builds sharpness. A taper (less training in the days before) brings freshness.

words.name: Sharp
words.text: Your legs know race pace and you're fairly fresh.
words.helps: A few easy days before the race, with one short sharp session, tops it up.

words.name: OK
words.text: Nothing special either way. You'd race to your normal level.
words.helps: Race-specific sessions (800 m intervals, club sessions, speed & strides) raise sharpness; rest and easy days raise freshness.

words.name: Rusty
words.text: You haven't done much race-pace work lately, so you'd run a little below your level.
words.helps: Sessions at race pace (800 m intervals, club group sessions, speed & strides) and racing itself bring sharpness back within a week or two.

tired.name: Tired
tired.text: You're carrying too much fatigue to race at your best, so you'd run below your level.
tired.helps: Easy days and rest days bring freshness back. A taper before a big race does the same.
